title: System theme, dark mode and status bar colors on phones
when: The phone app should follow the system light or dark setting, including the browser bar, status bar, splash and form controls, without a white flash.
prompt:
Goal: The whole phone chrome (page, status bar, browser bar, native controls) switches with the system theme and stays in sync with a manual choice.
Steps:
1. <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> and CSS :root { color-scheme: light dark; } so scrollbars and inputs follow the theme.
2. Two theme-color metas: <meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" content="#ffffff"> and one for dark with the dark header color.
3. Tokens in :root and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { ... } }, plus [data-theme="dark"] for a manual override.
4. Set data-theme from storage in a tiny inline script in head before CSS paints, to avoid a flash on launch.
5. Listen to matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").addEventListener("change", apply) when the choice is "system".
6. Capacitor: in apply() call StatusBar.setStyle({ style: dark ? Style.Dark : Style.Light }) and StatusBar.setBackgroundColor where supported.
7. The manifest background_color is used for the splash; pick a neutral that suits both themes.
Quality bar:
- No white flash when launching in dark mode.
- Status bar icons stay readable on both themes.
Pitfalls:
- Updating CSS but not the theme-color meta.
- Pure black and pure white text, which smear on OLED screens; use near black and off white.
Verify:
- [ ] color-scheme meta and CSS property present.
- [ ] Dark tokens under prefers-color-scheme.
- [ ] A change listener updates the bars.
Output: head tags in index.html, theme.css and theme.js.

examples.input: meu app fica branco piscando no modo escuro do celular
examples.output: color-scheme meta, two theme-color metas, inline theme script, StatusBar style synced
